name: Aida Impact challenges 2026
summary: AIDA invites students, researchers, developers, designers, and innovators to develop AI-powered solutions that improve accessibility and empower people with disabilities
benefits: Compete against teams worldwide
Exhibit projects to thousands of visitors
Career and networking support
eligibility: National and International Undergraduate Individuals.
Special Priorities to a team consisting of at least one member with disability
requirements: Submission fee of Rs. 5000 for innovation challenge / Rs. 2000 for research challenge per team
timeline: Applications open on 13 September and close on 16 October 2026. Semifinalists are announced on 6 November, followed by workshops, mentorship, and the ideathon. The Grand Finale takes place in Kathmandu from 17-19 December 2026.

name: Mini Research / Faculty Research Proposals, FY 2083/84 BS
organizer: Birendra Multiple Campus, Research Management Cell (Tribhuvan University)
summary: Birendra Multiple Campus invites its faculty to submit Mini Research / Faculty Research proposals for FY 2083/84 BS. Proposals are sent by email with a scanned copy of the Rs. 1000 fee receipt.
benefits: Promotion and recognition
A research record
eligibility: Faculty members of Birendra Multiple Campus
requirements: Submission fee of Rs. 1000/-, paid at the account section of the Campus, with a scanned copy of the receipt sent by email
Similarity index must be less than 15%
Proposal format as prescribed by the Tribhuvan University Research Management Cell Guidelines 2082
timeline: Notice dated 22-06-2083 BS. Proposals are invited for FY 2083/84 BS. The submission deadline is Mangsir 14, 2083 BS (30 November 2026 AD).

contact.office: Research Management Cell, Birendra Multiple Campus, Bharatpur, Chitwan, Nepal

name: Google Summer of Code
summary: Work on a real open source project with mentors from the project for 12+ weeks, and get a stipend for it.
benefits: Stipend, paid after passing evaluations; the amount depends on your country
Mentorship from experienced maintainers
Project sizes of about 90, 175 or 350 hours
eligibility: 18 or older at registration
A student or an open source beginner
Accepted into GSoC no more than once before
Eligible to work in your country of residence
timeline: Contributor applications open in March. In 2026 they ran 16–31 March, and coding started 25 May.

name: Outreachy
summary: Paid three-month internships in open source and open science for people who are under-represented in tech.
benefits: US$7,000 total stipend
Three months of mentored work on an open source project
eligibility: Anyone who faces under-representation, systemic bias or discrimination in the technology industry of their country
Check the full eligibility rules on the Outreachy site before applying
timeline: Two cohorts a year. Applications open in early February (May–August internships) and early to mid August (December–March internships).

name: LFX Mentorship
summary: Mentored projects in Linux Foundation communities such as Kubernetes and the Linux kernel, three times a year.
benefits: Stipend that depends on your country, paid half at midterm and half at the end
12 weeks full-time or 24 weeks part-time
eligibility: 18 or older and legally able to work where you live
Not a previous or current Linux Foundation mentee
Apply to up to three programs per term and finish their prerequisite tasks
timeline: Three terms: Spring (March–May), Summer (June–August) and Fall (September–November).

name: MLH Fellowship
summary: A 12-week remote internship alternative where you build real projects with mentors from companies like GitHub, Meta and Google.
benefits: Educational stipend
Tracks in Software Engineering, Production Engineering (SRE) and Web3 Engineering
Professional mentors and a peer cohort
eligibility: See the MLH Fellowship FAQ for current requirements
timeline: Several start dates a year. Apply for an upcoming batch on the site.

name: Summer of Bitcoin
summary: A summer internship for university students to contribute code or design to Bitcoin open source projects.
benefits: Stipend of about US$6,600 paid in bitcoin, depending on location
Developer and designer tracks
A bootcamp before the project starts
eligibility: University students (undergraduate or graduate), 18 or older
No Bitcoin experience needed
timeline: Applications close in mid-February (15 February in 2026), followed by a bootcamp, proposals in April and coding from May to August.

name: IEEEXtreme 20.0
summary: A 24-hour global programming competition for teams of IEEE student members.
benefits: Compete against teams worldwide
Free to enter for IEEE student members
eligibility: IEEE Student membership is required to register
Teams are advised and proctored by an IEEE member
timeline: IEEEXtreme 20.0 takes place on 31 October 2026. Team and proctor registration is open.

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
summary: A month-long celebration of open source. In 2026 you take part through in-person Fests, online challenges and livestreams rather than pull requests.
benefits: Virtual stickers for taking part, and a physical sticker pack once you collect three
More swag for continued participation
More than 300 in-person Fests worldwide
eligibility: Open to everyone; sign in with a MyMLH account
Pull requests no longer count toward rewards
timeline: All of October 2026. The participant dashboard opened on 1 October.

name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
summary: The world's largest annual hackathon. Teams solve challenges using NASA's open data, online or at local events.
benefits: Work with NASA and partner space agency data
Global awards for winning teams
Local events have been held in Kathmandu in past years
eligibility: Anyone with an interest in space and science
timeline: 14–15 November 2026. Registration is open now.

name: ICPC
summary: The best-known programming contest for university teams, with regional rounds that lead to the World Finals.
benefits: Regional contests across Asia, with the best teams advancing to the World Finals
Teams from Nepal have competed in the Asia Dhaka regional
eligibility: Teams of three university students with a coach
Check the ICPC eligibility rules for year and age limits
timeline: Regional registrations usually open in August and September.

name: Advent of Code
summary: Daily programming puzzles in December that you can solve in any language. Great practice for DSA and for club challenges.
benefits: Free, any programming language
Private leaderboards for your class or club
eligibility: Everyone
timeline: Puzzles start on 1 December and now run until mid-December.

name: Kaggle Competitions
summary: Year-round data science and machine learning competitions, from beginner playgrounds to prize challenges.
benefits: Real datasets and public notebooks to learn from
Some competitions offer prize money
eligibility: Free account; each competition sets its own rules
timeline: Year-round.

name: GitHub Campus Experts
summary: A leadership program for students who build technical communities on their campus.
benefits: Training in public speaking, technical writing and community management
Support from GitHub for running campus events
eligibility: Enrolled students with a verified GitHub Education account
Application cycles are announced on GitHub Education
timeline: Applications open in cycles. Watch the GitHub Education students page.

name: Microsoft Student Ambassadors
summary: A student community for building AI skills and leadership. Since April 2026 anyone eligible can join without a competitive application.
benefits: Progress through Alpha, Beta and Gold milestones by running events, creating content and mentoring
Access to Microsoft developer tools and Azure credits
eligibility: Enrolled at an accredited academic institution
Check the official page for age and other requirements
timeline: Open sign-up, year-round.

name: Google Developer Groups on Campus
summary: University chapters for students who want to learn Google technologies and build projects together. Join a chapter or apply to lead one.
benefits: Workshops, study jams and solution challenges
Organizer training and a global network
eligibility: University students; organizers are selected per campus
timeline: Chapters choose new organizers each academic year.

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
summary: Free professional developer tools for verified students, including GitHub Copilot.
benefits: Partner offers on developer tools and services
GitHub Copilot free for verified students
Codespaces hours for cloud development
eligibility: 13 or older
Enrolled in a degree or diploma program
A school email address or official proof of enrollment
timeline: Apply any time.

name: Azure for Students
summary: Cloud credits and free services to learn and build on Microsoft Azure.
benefits: US$100 credit to use within 12 months
Free monthly amounts of popular services, renewable each year while you're a student
No credit card required
eligibility: Full-time university students at accredited institutions
Sign up with your school email
timeline: Apply any time.

name: AWS Educate
summary: Free cloud training with hands-on labs and badges, no credit card needed.
benefits: Self-paced training and hands-on labs
Shareable digital badges
Job board for learners 18 and older
eligibility: 13 or older; sign up with an email address
timeline: Join any time.

name: Annual Nepal AI School
summary: An 11-day in-person school with AI lectures, labs and project work, taught by researchers from around the world.
benefits: Lectures, hands-on labs and team projects
Scholarships for Nepali students
eligibility: Senior undergraduates, graduate and PhD students, faculty and industry professionals
timeline: 7th edition: 28 December 2026 – 7 January 2027 at Kathmandu World School, Suryabinayak, Bhaktapur. Nepal Student Scholarship deadline 31 October 2026; non-scholarship deadline 15 November 2026.

name: Fusemachines AI Fellowship
summary: A 24-week AI and data science program with a full scholarship for selected Nepali fellows.
benefits: Full scholarship
Microdegree in Artificial Intelligence (not university-accredited)
Capstone project and mentorship; evening classes
eligibility: Nepali nationals
Strong maths (linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics), Python and data structures
Pass an online entrance assessment and interview
timeline: Applications open early in the year. For 2026 the deadline was 20 March, with 100 seats.

name: Code for Nepal Data Fellowship
summary: Free AI and data science training through a premium DataCamp subscription, for Nepalis anywhere in the world.
benefits: DataCamp Premium access with courses and certificates
Chance to publish data stories on the Code for Nepal site
Career and networking support
eligibility: Nepalis in and outside Nepal
High school degree or above
timeline: The 2026 edition took applications from 5 July to 30 August for 1,000 participants. Watch for the next call.

name: LOCUS
summary: Nepal's national technology exhibition, run by Pulchowk Campus students since 2003, with project exhibitions, hackathons and competitions.
benefits: Exhibit projects to thousands of visitors
Hackathons such as Hack-A-Week and prize competitions
eligibility: Students from schools and colleges across Nepal
timeline: Held early each year. LOCUS 2026 ran 30 January – 1 February 2026.
